messages:
marie: heads up — since ~02:10 UTC we're getting reports that ipv6-only clients (mobile carrier NAT64) can't finish TLS to model-edge.redwood.internal. Looks like requests start but hang at handshake. only affects certain carriers in US-west.

sam: which LB are they hitting? nlb or alb?

marie: NLB in front of our edge pool in us-west-2. It's configured dual-stack but I see mixed DNS answers. Some carriers resolve only an A via our resolver, some get AAAA and attempt v6, then hang.

yusuf: can you paste a `dig +short` for the endpoint from a repro host? curious about AAAA TTLs.

marie: sure — from one of the affected probes:
```
$ dig +short AAAA model-edge.redwood.internal @1.1.1.1
2406:...:abcd::1
```
and for A:
```
$ dig +short A model-edge.redwood.internal @1.1.1.1
34.201.12.78
```
TTL for AAAA is 30s, for A is 300s.

alex: that low AAAA TTL rings a bell — our edge DNS updates (autoscaler reassigns instances) were recently changed to set shorter AAAA TTL to speed cutover. maybe carriers cache weirdly and NAT64 translation state expires?

sam: NAT64 doesn't need DNS TTL to function, but some carrier stacks create ephemeral state based on the AAAA mapping lifetime. If AAAA disappears and the client tries A via 464XLAT/NAT64 path, translation can collapse mid-connection.

marie: ops note — reproducer from carrier X shows SYN then immediate RST from the NLB's v6 path, but v4 cleanly succeeds if we force A-only.

yusuf: can we verify NLB has both target group healthchecks IPv4+IPv6? There was a config where the IPv6 listener forwarded to IPv4 targets and healthcheck probe used A-only which confused the NLB.

marie: checked — healthchecks were A-only for the v6 listener due to a longstanding terraform var default. Oops.

alex: nice find. Fix path: update terraform to enable dual-probe healthchecks, and bump the AAAA TTL to 60s while we roll. Also add a small fallback in the client routing rule to prefer A if v6 handshake failed within 1s.

sam: agree. Also let's add a transient traffic rule routing v6->v4 translation via our egress proxies when we detect repeated RSTs, to avoid user-visible failures. That should be hitless.

marie: on it — i'll open a PR to change the healthchecks and TTL. anyone object to 60s TTL?

yusuf: 60s SGTM. add a changelog note to the rollout and set a canary in us-west-2a first.

deploy-bot: deploy queued by marie — infra/edge-dns: ttl-bump + nlb-healthcheck-dualprobe (pr/4321).

alex: after deploy, i'll run synthetic probes from carrier X and carrier Y and post results here. If we still see >0.1% v6 failure rate, we'll enable the v6->v4 egress proxy rule.

marie: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/pr/4321 — includes terraform, runtime routing rule, and a short rollout playbook.

ops-bot: incident-note: created with sev-low; initial mitigation in progress.

sam: quick debugging note for posterity — avoid very low AAAA TTLs on dual-stack endpoints if you depend on carrier NAT64; carriers may treat AAAA churn as signal to rebuild translation state.

marie: thanks team. will update here after canary results (ETA ~20m).
